m1.summary:
M1 (database) for PR 6b-4 is built and pushed to co-001/pr-06b-mail-streams at head 356af63, in three commits: c203d7b, 7100d39 and 356af63.

What was built:
- **Migration** packages/db/migrations/20261107090000_mail_streams.sql. It was written through the new-migration marker route under the founder's standing permission. Each write or edit set the marker with a shell touch and removed it right after. No permission check refused it. The marker was never committed and no other migration was touched.
- **Tables:**
  - mail_recipient_key: one hex pepper, fixed.
  - mail_stream: three seeded rows, all sending and confirmed.
  - mail_send: one row per SES message ID. It holds no address and no hash of one. Kept 30 days on the screening stream and 90 days on the others.
  - screening_mail_refusal: the keyed hash of a refused address, kept 365 days (Q11 (b)).
  - screening_bounce_mark: 7-day marks (Q10 (a)).
  - support_grant_notice and support_grant_notice_recipient: registered tenant tables with forced RLS, a tenant policy, an owner policy, a restrictive read policy that mirrors support_grant's, and SELECT for tp_app.
  - dunning_notice_recipient: billing's, owner-only.
  - Changed tables: screening_run.client_subject, invitation.undelivered_at and undelivered_reason, the notification kind support_notice_undelivered, and an audit_event_record policy that reserves notice_undelivered, mail_stream_paused and mail_stream_resumed.
- **Triggers:** the screening refusals and the run's mail gate, in the order D2 pins.
- **Functions:** the design's section 3 functions, plus screening_mail_gate() for tp_screening only.
- **submit_screening():** recreated on 6b-3's body with client_subject added. A db test diffs the two bodies.
- **Dropped:** the three functions the outboxes replace.
- **Header:** says the migration is safe with the previous image running and lists five deploy-window effects.

packages/db changes:
- Drizzle schema in operations, tenancy, billing, onboarding, screening and index, with the closed-list constants.
- domain-model/areas.json places the new tables.
- New mail.db.test.ts (24 tests).
- screening.db.test.ts gains 8 tests: D7's body diff, D2's refusal order, the refusal list end to end, prospect links, the bounce budget, the spread pause and the run gate. It also tests closed-first in its setup.
- hardening.db.test.ts covers the reserved actions.
- Pinned lists updated in catalog.db.test.ts, location.db.test.ts, migrate.db.test.ts and screening-queue.db.test.ts.
- row-factory.ts now handles a foreign key paired with practice_id. It is not in my file list, but nobody else owns it, and the cross-tenant test needed it.

Docs:
- ADR 0065 is new. It records the founder's Q1, Q9, Q10 (a), Q11 (b) and Q12 rulings of 2026-10-21. Its "Revisit when" also records the capacity decision you asked to keep in view: the free runner with advisory time on pull requests was chosen to save cost, to be revisited before the screening opens and once production has traffic (GitHub issue #41, ADR 0062).
- data-retention.md gains every value the mail path keeps.
- domain-model.md is regenerated on a fresh PostgreSQL 18 database. Its SHA-256 is 07c4a8eeca46ef5f2fdbc0974f23c4bf0ebb257f79fd7cc2b7bef8a1735d5b31 and the approval line is line 7327, left blank.
- The Cross-checks block shows 97 Drizzle tables and 97 migrated tables, nothing missing on either side, 0 column differences and 0 catalog problems. No false difference.
- data-dictionary.md is unchanged: it stays a verbatim import (reconciliation-001 D2 (a)), and the domain model records the new tables.

The ADR 0062 "Revisit when" entry itself was not written. ADR 0062 is M3's file under the plan's ownership, so the capacity note lives in ADR 0065 for now (see open items).

differences_from_design: The refusal gate is a trigger on screening_upload (screening_upload_mail_gate, BEFORE INSERT WHEN status = 'accepted'), not screening_prospect_mail_gate on screening_prospect. reject_screening_upload() also inserts a prospect, and a refused upload is never emailed; D9 says no address check runs for an upload that fails the row checks. The D2 order still holds because the upload is inserted before the run inside submit_screening().

screening_prospect_mail_forget is not created, although the plan and task list it. Design D13 creates it only under Q11's alternative, and the founder chose 12 months, so the trigger would do nothing.

client_subject is the last parameter, after request, with DEFAULT NULL, so the previous web's 30-argument call still works in the deploy window. It is nullable because the web has no client address without a trusted proxy; a run without one is held to its account's budget alone.
The bounce budget refuses at 3 live marks on either the account subject (screening_run.rate_subject from 6b-3) or the client subject. There is no prospect column (section 5, D6).

support_grant_notice_recipient has an id uuid primary key and UNIQUE (notice_id, user_id) (support_grant_notice_recipient_once), because the generated cross-tenant tests need a single-column key. The composite foreign key (notice_id, practice_id) to support_grant_notice is kept, and the row factory was extended for it.
The pepper is stored as 64 hex characters (text) and decoded in mail_recipient_sha256(). Drizzle and the domain model's cross-check have no bytea type.
Both notice tables also have a restrictive tp_app SELECT policy that mirrors support_grant's: the practice's owning group, or a platform administrator.

All three mail_stream rows are seeded with ses_enabled_confirmed_at = now(): no stream has been paused yet. The reconcile clears it if SES reads the set disabled. In production and staging the screening still opens only once the probes have returned.
Readiness needs the delivered and bounced probes within 48 hours and since the last resume. The design said only within 48 hours; its e2e journey expects probes after a resume.

probe_due and probe_missed track an outstanding probe. A probe is due daily once the last one came back, at once after a resume, and again when one has been unanswered for 26 hours, which also sets probe_missed.
The invitation flag is set only by kind cognito on the transactional stream. The design said any transactional message; only Cognito's message is an invitation.

Parameter names differ where the design's clash: operator_open_support_notice(target, ...), because grant is a reserved word, and the billing functions use (target_invoice, notice_stage, ...). operator_record_mail_event's notice_undelivered returns the support grant's ID, which is what NOTICE_UNDELIVERED logs.
console_pause_mail_stream accepts only stream 'screening' and reason 'operator'. console_resume_mail_stream accepts cause_fixed or false_alarm.
The CHECK on mail_send is named mail_send_expiry_window; the trigger keeps the name mail_send_expiry.
Added guards: mail_recipient_key_fixed and mail_recipient_key_no_truncate (the pepper never changes), screening_run_client_subject_fixed, and updated_at triggers on the new tables.

screening_mail_sending(), mail_recipient_sha256() and every helper or trigger function are SECURITY INVOKER with no grant. 6b-3's screening test requires that every function a role may call runs as the owner and no other does.
An undelivered complaint is not counted as undelivered for the outboxes: a complaint means the message arrived. Undelivered is bounced, suppressed, rejected or failed.
failure_code keeps the SES error name when it matches ^[A-Za-z]{1,64}$ and stores 'Unrecognized' otherwise.
NOTIFICATION_KINDS gains follow_up and support_notice_undelivered. The other catalog.ts lists are unchanged; only the test lists grew.
screening-queue.db.test.ts (6b-3's D7 test) now compares the live body with client_subject stripped. The full diff against 20261106090000 is in screening.db.test.ts.
data-dictionary.md is unchanged: it stays a verbatim import (reconciliation-001 D2 (a)).

FUNCTIONS (all SET search_path = pg_catalog, public, pg_temp; REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC). Errors are SQLSTATE 23514 with the constraint name shown unless stated.

tp_screening (the consumer):
- screening_mail_gate() RETURNS TABLE(sending boolean, resumed_at timestamptz). Read it before claiming. If sending is false, finish without claiming. Log "emailed after waiting" for a run whose received_at is before resumed_at.

tp_app (the web):
- screening_mail_status() RETURNS TABLE(paused boolean, ready boolean). paused means screeningOpen() returns {open:false, reason:'mail_paused'}. ready is false in production or staging means not_ready; dev ignores ready. ready needs sending plus a delivered and a bounced probe within 48 hours and since resumed_at. A missing row reads paused and not ready.
- submit_screening(practice text, state_code text, zip5 text, plus_four text, email text, codes text[], modifier_sets text[], unit_counts integer[], places text[], products text[], bands text[], allowed_cents bigint[], claim_counts integer[], rows_left_out integer, claim_lines_left_out integer, allowed_cents_left_out bigint, rows_outside_content integer, claim_lines_outside_content bigint, allowed_cents_outside_content bigint, heard_from text, campaign_source text, campaign_medium text, campaign_name text, click_kind text, firm text, consent_sha256 text, terms_sha256 text, received timestamptz, rate_account_subject text, request text, client_subject text DEFAULT NULL) RETURNS uuid.
  - The web passes $31 = rateSubjectHash(sealer, 'screening', 'address', clientAddress) as 64 lowercase hex, or null when there is no client address.
  - Refusals, in order: screening_closed; screening_zip_unknown, screening_zip_plus_four, screening_zip_plus_four_unknown, screening_locality_not_loaded; screening_rows; screening_band_outside_content; screening_paused; screening_contact_undeliverable; screening_bounce_budget. A malformed subject raises screening_run_client_subject.
- console_mail_streams() RETURNS TABLE(stream, paused_at, paused_reason, paused_by, pause_sends, pause_bounces, pause_complaints, window_starts_at, window_sends, window_bounces, window_complaints, resumed_at, confirmed_at, sending boolean, ready boolean, probe_sent_at, probe_delivered_at, probe_bounced_at, client_marks int, account_marks int).
- console_pause_mail_stream(stream text, reason text) RETURNS boolean. stream must be 'screening' (else mail_stream_only_screening_pauses); reason must be 'operator' (else mail_stream_paused_reason).
- console_resume_mail_stream(stream text, reason text) RETURNS boolean. reason is cause_fixed or false_alarm (else mail_stream_resume_reason). Returns false when the stream is not paused.
- console_mail_undelivered(since timestamptz) RETURNS TABLE(stream, kind, state, recipient_user_id, practice_id, subject_id, undelivered_at, messages int). Null since means 7 days. At most 500 customer rows. Screening rows are counted by kind and state, never listed.
- The four console functions need a person with feature_flag.manage; otherwise 42501.
- console_support_grants(): its first 9 columns are unchanged. It adds opened_recipients, opened_delivered, opened_undelivered, opened_pending (integer) and opened_sent_at (timestamptz), and the same five closed_* columns. Recipients is null when the notice has not been opened, and 0 means the practice had no administrator.

Tables tp_app reads directly, under app.practice_ids, as the owning group or a platform administrator:
- support_grant_notice(id, support_grant_id, practice_id, notice, recipients, created_at, undelivered_reported_at, updated_at).
- support_grant_notice_recipient(id, notice_id, practice_id, user_id, ses_message_id, state [pending|sent|delayed|delivered|complained|bounced|suppressed|rejected|failed], attempts, next_attempt_at, failure_code, sent_at, updated_at).
- invitation.undelivered_at and invitation.undelivered_reason [bounced|suppressed|rejected|complained]. Show the flag while undelivered_at >= sent_at - 5 s.
- Notification kind support_notice_undelivered: subject_id is the support_grant_notice id; counts and totals_cents are {}.

tp_operator (the platform's mail_events and mail_expiry jobs):
- operator_record_mail_event(message_id text, stream text, event text, mail_at timestamptz, event_at timestamptz, recipient text, kind text, subject uuid, recipient_user uuid, practice uuid, bounce_kind text, bounce_subtype text, complaint_type text, request text) RETURNS TABLE(recorded boolean, state text, notice_undelivered uuid, invoice_undelivered uuid, invitation_undelivered uuid, stream_paused text).
  - notice_undelivered is a support_grant id.
  - Run it in a transaction with app.practice_ids = '{tp_practice}' when the tag is present (required for kinds support_grant_opened and support_grant_closed; otherwise 42501), else '{}'.
  - event: send, delivery_delay, delivery, bounce, complaint, reject, rendering_failure.
  - bounce_kind: permanent, transient, undetermined; unknown becomes undetermined.
  - bounce_subtype is SES's subtype snake-cased: general, no_email, suppressed, on_account_suppression_list, on_configuration_set_suppression_list, mailbox_full, message_too_large, content_rejected, attachment_rejected; anything else is other.
  - complaint_type: abuse, auth_failure, fraud, not_spam, virus, other, unspecified; null becomes unspecified, unknown becomes other.
  - kind is the tp_kind tag. Cognito's untagged mail on the transactional set is kind 'cognito' with subject null; probes are kind 'probe' with subject null.
  - subject is the tp_subject tag: the notice row id, invoice id, digest id, or screening run id. recipient_user is tp_recipient.
  - recipient is the destination address. It is used only to resolve a Cognito user and to hash a refused screening address.
  - Errors: mail_event_type and mail_event_sent_at; mail_send CHECK names such as mail_send_stream_kind, mail_send_subject and mail_send_message_id (^[A-Za-z0-9-]{20,100}$); 23503 for an unknown stream.
  - A repeated or lower-ranked event returns recorded=false.
- operator_mail_account_signal(signal text, request text) RETURNS boolean. signal: bounce_rate_alarm or complaint_rate_alarm (pauses for account_rate), enforcement_not_healthy (account_review). Anything else raises mail_account_signal. True when this call paused the stream.
- operator_mail_streams() RETURNS TABLE(stream, paused, confirmed, probe_due, probe_missed).
- operator_mail_stream_confirmed(stream text, enabled boolean) RETURNS boolean (confirmed after the call). It never confirms while paused.
- operator_mail_probe_sent(stream text) RETURNS void.
- operator_mail_expire(at_most integer) RETURNS integer. at_most must be at least 1.
- operator_open_support_notice(target uuid, notice text, request text) RETURNS TABLE(notice_id uuid, recipients integer, opened boolean). Needs the notice's practice scope. recipients=0 with opened=true means log NOTICE_UNDELIVERABLE.
- operator_support_notices_pending(at_most integer) RETURNS TABLE(notice_id, practice_id, user_id, support_grant_id, notice). No scope needed. Openings come first.
- operator_support_notice_claim(notice uuid, recipient uuid) RETURNS TABLE(email text, reads bigint). Needs scope. Zero rows means skip. Locks the recipient row FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
- operator_support_notice_sent(notice uuid, recipient uuid, message_id text, request text) RETURNS boolean. Call it in the claim's transaction after SES accepts. Raises support_grant_notice_recipient_sent if the row is not pending. True means log NOTICE_UNDELIVERED.
- operator_support_notice_failed(notice uuid, recipient uuid, error_name text, permanent boolean, request text) RETURNS boolean. Call it in a new transaction. Retries come after 1, 5, 15 and 60 minutes; the fifth attempt, or a permanent error, fails it. True means log NOTICE_UNDELIVERED.
- operator_due_support_notices(integer) keeps its signature.
- Dropped: operator_record_support_notice(uuid,text,text), operator_practice_administrator_emails(uuid), billing_owner_emails(uuid).

tp_billing:
- billing_open_dunning_notice(target_invoice uuid, notice_stage text, request text) RETURNS TABLE(recipients integer, opened boolean). Stages: payment_failed, second_notice, third_notice, final_notice, suspended, reinstated (never resolved). Call it in the stage transaction. recipients=0 means NOTICE_UNDELIVERABLE.
- billing_dunning_notices_pending(at_most integer) RETURNS TABLE(invoice_id, stage, organization_id, user_id).
- billing_dunning_notice_claim(target_invoice uuid, notice_stage text, recipient uuid) RETURNS TABLE(email text).
- billing_dunning_notice_sent(target_invoice, notice_stage, recipient, message_id text, request text) RETURNS boolean. Raises dunning_notice_recipient_sent if not pending.
- billing_dunning_notice_failed(target_invoice, notice_stage, recipient, error_name text, permanent boolean, request text) RETURNS boolean.
- In both, true means log NOTICE_UNDELIVERED with invoice_id.

Granted to no role:
- mail_recipient_sha256(text): the keyed hash, sha256(decode(pepper,'hex') || lower(btrim(address))) as hex.
- screening_mail_sending(), mail_state_rank(text), mail_window_counts(text), mail_stream_pause(text,uuid,text), support_notice_administrators(uuid), support_notice_report_undelivered(uuid,text), support_notice_counts(uuid,text), dunning_notice_report_undelivered(uuid,text,text).

TRIGGERS:
- screening_upload_mail_gate: BEFORE INSERT ON screening_upload WHEN status = 'accepted'. Raises screening_paused, then screening_contact_undeliverable.
- screening_run_bounce_budget: BEFORE INSERT ON screening_run. Raises screening_bounce_budget at 3 live marks on rate_subject or client_subject.
- screening_run_mail_gate: BEFORE UPDATE OF status ON screening_run. Raises screening_mail_paused on a claim, completion or failure while not sending, so operator_screening_claim, _complete and _fail raise it. A recorded batch is allowed.

- screening_run_client_subject_fixed, mail_recipient_key_fixed, mail_recipient_key_no_truncate.

STREAMS AND STATE:
- Streams: transactional, notices, screening; only screening pauses.
- Pause reasons: bounce_rate, complaint_rate, account_rate, account_review, operator.
- Cut-off (MAIL_CUTOFF): bounces*10000 > 300*max(sends,200), or complaints*100000 > 80*max(sends,2500), over the window from the later of now() - 7 days and window_starts_at.
- Seeds: all three streams unpaused and confirmed, so tests and the capacity harness run sending. A ready screening for production or staging needs the owner to set probe_delivered_at and probe_bounced_at to now(), or to record two probe events.

AUDIT:
- notice_undelivered: system, object support_grant with purpose = notice, or object invoice with purpose = stage.
- mail_stream_paused: object mail_stream, purpose = reason; system for the cut-off, user for the console.
- mail_stream_resumed: user, purpose cause_fixed or false_alarm.
- notice_sent: written at the first accepted send.

m2.summary:
M2 (worker) for PR 6b-4 is built, committed and pushed. Your capacity request is covered: ADR 0062's "Revisit when" now records the decision (free runner, time advisory, chosen to save cost). It points to GitHub issue #41 to revisit before the screening opens and once production has traffic, by measuring on AWS staging or an organization's 8-core runner, then the sizing question O9. M3 added it in 6851bde; M2 did not edit ADR 0062.

What M2 built:
- Every email now has exactly one recipient. It goes through its stream's SES configuration set (`<MAIL_STREAM_PREFIX>-<stream>`) and carries its identity as SES tags (tp_kind, tp_subject, tp_practice, tp_recipient), never an address. A tag value failing ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$ is refused before anything is sent. Senders return SES's message ID.
- The screening's email comes from its own sender (SCREENING_MAIL_FROM, shown as "PaidWhole"), with Reply-To set to SCREENING_REPLY_TO.
- The local sender still writes `to` as a one-element array, so existing outbox readers keep exact matching. When MAIL_EVENTS_DIR is set, it also writes the events SES's simulator would send.
- A new events parser reads SES events and the two account alarms. It never reads a bounce's diagnosticCode, and snake-cases bounce subtypes and complaint types.
- New platform job mail_events, every minute:
  - keeps the screening's SES set matching the database (disabled while paused, re-disabled if something re-enables it, enabled then confirmed after a resume; the other two sets are never touched);
  - sends daily probes only to SES's simulator, only after the identities are verified;
  - drains the SQS queue (at most 1,000 messages or 50 s), recording each event once per message, in any order, and deleting it from the queue only after the record commits;
  - pauses the screening stream on an account alarm or unhealthy SES enforcement, and logs IDs and codes only.
- New nightly mail_expiry job (03:50 UTC) deletes expired mail records.
- Support-access notices and dunning notices now go from recorded outboxes: one message per recipient, each in its own transaction. A failed send is recorded in a new transaction and retried after 1, 5, 15 and 60 minutes; retries reach only recipients still pending, and a permanent SES refusal fails at once. A notice with no administrator records notice_undelivered and never notice_sent.
- New dunning_notices job every minute sends the dunning retries; the daily billing_dunning job opens each stage's outbox and sends at once.
- The monthly digest is tagged and goes on the transactional stream.
- Screening consumer:
  - It reads screening_mail_gate() inside the claim's transaction. A run found not sending is not claimed and spends no attempt; the job ends 'mail_paused' with "screening run waits: email paused" (SCREENING_MAIL_PAUSED).
  - Neither sweep sends or fails anything while the stream is not sending.
  - If the database refuses (screening_mail_paused) or SES refuses (SendingPausedException), the step rolls back and the run is left as it was; the stale rule picks it up after the resume.
  - A run received before the stream's last resume is logged "screening result emailed after waiting", which keeps it out of the 60-second metric.
- Capacity harness:
  - It seeds the screening stream sending and ready, and gives the web MAIL_CHECK_DELAY_MS=2000, so every upload's time to email includes the address checks' worst case (G1).
  - The report gains `mail` {addressCheckMs, screeningReady, heldLines}. The verdict fails a run whose checks weren't charged, whose stream wasn't ready, or whose consumer logged a run held by the mail gate.
- ADRs 0014, 0019 and 0050 are amended and ADR 0039 has a note.

**Infra (4e4a90f, b7df9e2)**
- The stack now owns three SES configuration sets: transactional, notices and screening.
- It owns two identities, MailFromAddress's domain and `screening.<domain>`, verified in two phases behind `MailIdentitiesVerified`.
- Mail events reach an encrypted queue with a dead-letter queue. Only the two rules can write to them.
- An SQS endpoint is added, limited to this account's queues.
- 15 alarms are wired, the SES grants are narrowed per set, and the screening role can use only its own identity and set.
- New since the summary: the database parameter group sets `log_parameter_max_length` and `log_parameter_max_length_on_error` to 0, so no bind value reaches the database log. This holds open item O11 in the template instead of a hand check.

**Web (89998f4)**
- Address checks in order: a typo hint and an unknown-ending warning in the browser, then the upload's own checks and the rate limit, then the same hints on the server, then DNS and SES validation together. SES validation is capped at 1,000 a day in production and 50 in staging.
- Every refused address gets one sentence.
- The screening closes while its mail stream is paused (everywhere) or not proven ready (staging and production).
- The web passes the client's keyed subject to `submit_screening` for the bounce budget.
- The kept refused-address sentence is added to four places: the upload form's hint, the "sent" alert, the closed-link page and the result page with no request.
- A new `/console/mail` page lets a platform administrator pause and resume the screening stream with a reason.
- Support-access notice delivery shows on the grant page and the console's support list; a notification links to the grant.
- The users page flags an undelivered invitation.
- The paused wording and the address wording are now two legal surfaces (`screening-mail-paused`, `screening-mail-address`), so production's screening stays closed until counsel's review is recorded.
- Two e2e journeys: the cut-off (SCR-21) and an undelivered notice (SEC-19).
- A new `mail-routes.db.test.ts` covers the console routes, notice states, notifications and invitations.
- The typo hints now name only the provider domain or the endings, so no form issue or error carries an address.

**Docs (b6d1c9c, 6851bde)**
- New `docs/runbooks/deliverability.md`.
- `docs/runbooks/deploy-and-rollback.md` gains the two mail phases, a launch checklist (O5, O11, O14) and rollback across PR 6b-4.
- Amendments to ADRs 0049, 0055 and 0062. ADR 0062 also records the capacity decision under "Revisit when", pointing to issue #41.
- Test matrix rows SCR-21, SCR-22, SEC-18, SEC-19 and JOB-05, with the synth matrix, registry and generated expected files kept in step.

pr.smoke:
Indicative only. This was a local process-runtime run on a 4-CPU container: advisory mode, S1 and S4, with the address checks charged at 2,000 ms on every upload (G1). Seconds to email:
- S1-1: 27.5. S1-2: 2.6.
- S4#1: 34.1, 32.8, 31.4 and 23.5 (small).
- S4#2: 33.3, 29.4, 32.6 and 21.1.
- S4#3: 36.8, 33.6, 34.1 and 25.3.

The middle run is S4#1, whose worst upload took 34.1 s. There were no time warnings: every upload stayed under the 48-s line and the 44-s question. The release took 301.8 s to load.

Every correctness check held:
- Every upload was emailed in the normal tier.
- S1-1 matches the frozen oracle and S1-2 matches the whole-release oracle.
- The large uploads were queued after 5.6 to 8.1 s, with the small one behind them.
- No OOM kill and no limit reached. The consumer peaked at 1,150 of 4,096 MiB and the web at 326 of 1,024 MiB.
- Mail: addressCheckMs 2000, screeningReady true, heldLines 0.

The verdict says 'fail (time advisory)'. Every reason is something this kind of run cannot meet, not a bug: it ran only two scenarios, the process runtime's Postgres has no limits applied and no cold start, and the S2-1 and S3-1 oracles were not run. The report is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e7bf8d14-3b4c-5e38-9cea-a1f92a95083e/scratchpad/pr6b4/smoke1/summary.md.

open_items: Your capacity note is recorded. ADR 0062's "Revisit when" (M3, 6851bde) and ADR 0065 point to GitHub issue #41. The free runner with time advisory on PRs was chosen to save cost. Revisit before the screening opens and once production has traffic, by measuring on AWS staging or an 8-core runner, then settle sizing question O9. I added the same note, with the 2026-10-21 rulings, to reconciliation-001 (6579169). No builder had written it there, though the computed task required it.
The founder approves the domain model's SHA-256 only after the review round. Until then CI fails the approval case of domain-model.db.test.ts, as expected.
The review round has not run yet. It is two adversarial reviews, one using the security-reviewer checklist (G5: IAM, addresses, reserved audit actions).

Residuals for the reviewers, all from my read of the diffs: (a) a run completion that commits just before a concurrent pause still sends, until the platform disables the SES set within a minute. (b) Someone who types a mailbox they know is valid and gets refused can infer that it bounced or was reported as spam on the screening stream in the last 12 months. This needs counsel, with O4. (c) A failure notice sent after the failure commits can be lost to a pause that lands in between. (d) The harness's addressCheckMs is the configured delay, not a measured one, and the charge is skipped past the stand-in's daily cap of 50. This holds today at about 20 uploads per database.

Founder actions: phase 1 deploy, then DNS records from the stack's outputs (DKIM, MAIL FROM MX and SPF, DMARC). Phase 2 with MailIdentitiesVerified=true. SES production access. Postmaster Tools and SNDS (O5, O14). Staging checks after phase 2 (O11). Re-read the AWS prices (O12).
Counsel (O4): the paused page, the refused-address sentences, the bounce-budget refusal and the refusal-hash sentence, before the screening opens.
PR 6e (O13): reminders on the screening stream must read the mail gate and the refusal list. Also List-Unsubscribe headers, and whether reminders stay on tp_operator.
Plan O15: refresh the TLD snapshot and the typo list every quarter. Q13 belongs to the billing PR.
Doc nit in M3's file, reported and not fixed: docs/runbooks/deliverability.md section 2 step 5 says "Q1 (b)" for the SES plan; it should say Q1 (f).

Differences from the design, listed in the PR body: the refusal gate sits on accepted screening_upload rows, not on screening_prospect. screening_prospect_mail_forget is not created (the founder chose Q11 (b)). Only screening_run.client_subject was added, as the last parameter with default null. screening_mail_gate is granted to tp_screening only and screening_mail_sending to no role. The helper functions are invoker functions, not definers. data-dictionary.md is unchanged. The pepper comes from gen_random_uuid. RDS log_parameter_max_length is set to 0. The builders' reports arrived truncated, so any further departures are in ADR 0065's Alternatives table.
CI on draft PR 42 runs what was not run locally: the full test:db, e2e, golden and the advisory capacity workflow.
